_comment: Friendly emulation settings catalog, keyed by CORE (not platform) because core option keys differ per core. 'common' settings are frontend concepts applied to every core (rewind, aspect ratio, ...). Each 'cores.<coreName>' entry has 'settings' (friendly, shown in the UI) and 'defaults' (Firelight's opinionated overrides of the core's own raw option defaults). A friendly setting with a 'mapping' drives one or more core options ('values' maps friendly value -> core value; omit for identity, and omit 'mapping' entirely when the setting's own key IS the core option key). 'visibleWhen'/'enabledWhen' gate a setting on other settings' values (clauses AND-ed; a clause holds when the named setting is one of 'values').
_types_comment: 'type' accepts author-friendly aliases: 'boolean'/'toggle' -> BOOLEAN; 'options'/'dropdown' -> OPTIONS (needs 'options'); 'integer'/'slider' -> INTEGER (slider); 'number'/'spinbox' -> INTEGER (spinbox); 'custom' -> CUSTOM (needs an explicit 'widget' naming a QML delegate, e.g. 'gbc-palette'); 'game-picker' -> OPTIONS dropdown whose options are the user's eligible library games (filled in at runtime; the stored value is the chosen game's content hash); 'text' -> STRING free-text field (optional 'placeholder'); 'color' -> STRING hex color (optional 'options' as preset swatches); 'file'/'file-picker' -> STRING filesystem path (optional 'extensions' array, no dot); 'folder'/'folder-picker' -> STRING directory path; 'multi-select' -> OPTIONS checklist over 'options' whose value is a JSON array of selected option values. An explicit 'widget' overrides the derived control. Slider/number settings take 'min', 'max', and 'step' (all numeric). 'step' may be fractional (e.g. 0.25 -> float slider), a whole number other than 1 (e.g. 5 -> increments of 5), and defaults to 1 when omitted. A 'game-picker' takes 'eligiblePlatformIds' (array of platform ids; omit for any platform).

common.label: Rewind
common.description: Allow rewinding gameplay. Disabled in RetroAchievements hardcore mode.

common.label: Automatic save
common.description: Periodically write battery/SRAM to disk while playing.

common.label: Sync method
common.description: How gameplay is paced. Audio keeps the sound buffer full (smoothest audio, low CPU, works on any display); Sync to monitor matches your display's refresh rate when it's close to the game's and resamples audio to it (smoothest video); Native timer paces to the core's native rate; Fixed framerate paces to a rate you choose.

common.label: Target framerate
common.description: Frames per second to target when using Fixed framerate sync.

common.label: Dynamic rate control
common.description: Continuously micro-adjusts the audio resample rate to keep the sound buffer near half full, correcting slow drift so audio doesn't gradually crackle or desync over long sessions. Turn off to let the emulation pacer manage the buffer on its own.

common.label: Instant replay recording
common.description: Continuously records the last several seconds of gameplay in the background so you can save a clip of a moment that already happened with the clip shortcut. Clips are recorded at normal speed regardless of fast-forward or slow-motion. Uses extra CPU while a game is running; leave off if you don't capture clips.

common.label: Pointer speed (gamepad aim)
common.description: How fast the left analog stick glides the on-screen cursor when a controller is used as a mouse or light gun.

common.label: Aim light guns with the mouse
common.description: When on, the mouse aims and fires any light-gun or mouse device a game uses, even if a gamepad is selected for that player. Turn off to use only the selected controller.

gambatte_libretro._note: Game Boy / Game Boy Color. These friendly settings use the core key directly (identity); no 'mapping' needed.

settings.label: Color palette
settings.description: Palette used for original Game Boy games.

mgba_libretro._note: Game Boy Advance. Demonstrates a friendly setting that MAPS to a core key with value translation, plus a dependency.

settings.label: Color correction
settings.description: Simulate the GBA screen's washed-out colors.

mupen64plus_next_libretro._note: Nintendo 64. 'transfer-pak-game' demonstrates a library-sourced game picker (the value is stored but not yet consumed by emulation).

settings.label: Transfer Pak cartridge
settings.description: The Game Boy / Game Boy Color cartridge inserted into the controller's Transfer Pak.
